title: Fixed Array Range Totals
statement:
Build a helper that answers many "what is the total of this stretch?" questions about one array that never changes.

  • RangeTotals(nums) stores the array.
  • total(left, right) returns nums[left] + nums[left + 1] + … + nums[right]. Both ends are included, and 0 ≤ left ≤ right < nums.length.

There can be as many queries as there are elements, so each query should be fast.

Tests are a list of operations and their arguments; the first operation creates the object. The expected output has one entry per operation (null for the constructor).

examples.why: 4 − 2 + 7 = 9; −2 + 7 + 1 = 6; a one-element range is just that element.
Both ends count. Excluding the right end would give 6 and 0.

hints: Summing the range on every call is O(n) per query. The array never changes, so what can you prepare once?
If you knew the total of every prefix, how would you get the total of a middle stretch from two of them?
Store pre[i] = sum of the first i elements, with pre[0] = 0. Then total(l, r) = pre[r + 1] − pre[l].

explain.intuition:
The array is fixed, so do the work once up front. A prefix-sum array holds, at index i, the total of everything before position i. The sum of nums[l..r] is "everything up to r" minus "everything before l": pre[r + 1] − pre[l].

It is the same idea as a running balance in a bank statement: to know how much you spent between two dates, subtract the two balances instead of adding up every transaction again.
pitfalls: Using pre[r] − pre[l], which drops nums[r]. The extra leading 0 is what makes the inclusive formula clean.
Making pre the same length as nums and then special-casing l = 0 everywhere.
Recomputing anything inside total. All the work belongs in the constructor.

complexity.time: O(n) to build, O(1) per query

solutions.title: Sum on every query
solutions.idea: Loop from left to right on each call.

solutions.title: Prefix sums
solutions.idea: Precompute running totals once; each query is the difference of two of them.

followups: Values can now change between queries. Which structure keeps both updates and range totals at O(log n)?
Answer the same questions for a 2D grid of numbers and rectangular regions.
